title: Unravelling Specific Binding sites of Pulmonary Surfactants on Coronavirus Spike Protein Receptor-Binding Domain
authors: Kolattukudy P. Santo; Ryan Jaworski; Alexander V. Neimark
one_liner_zh: 该文用多尺度MD模拟研究肺表面活性剂脂质与SARS-CoV2刺突蛋白RBD的结合位点，虽涉及蛋白-配体互作建模，但对象为病毒蛋白-脂质而非蛋白质-DNA，且无TF-DNA或核酸互作内容，仅方法可部分借鉴。
abstract: The lung surfactant (LS) coating the alveoli is the first barrier to the airborne pathogens, such as coronaviruses, which may prevent lung infection. It is essential to understand the interactions of virion structural units with LS for efficient pharmaceutical design and formulation. Since LS is an inevitable encounter, both inhibitory as well as faciliatory interactions of the LS lipids with virion proteins and envelope play a crucial role in the virus’s fate in the respiratory system. In this work, by means of multiscale molecular dynamics simulations, we investigate the interactions of five LS lipids with the receptor binding domain (RBD) of the SARS-CoV2 Spike protein. By performing coarse-grained (CG) simulations of spontaneous protein-ligand binding, we identify six potential surfactant binding sites (SBS) on the RBD protein. We find that all surfactants bind to the binding pocket identified as the fatty acid binding site (FABS) that has allosteric effects on RBD-ACE2 binding. CG simulations reveal that FABS is most probable binding site for several phospholipids and cholesterol. Subsequent atomistic simulations of the back-transformed CG bound poses reveal high surfactant binding energies (27-58 kcal/mol) at FABS and surfactant-selective behavior of FABS-bound protein-surfactant complexes. Our analysis predicts that while anionic lipids POPG and POPI (palmitoyl oleoyl phosphatidyl glycerol/Inositol) may possess inhibitory effects, DPPC (dipalmitoyl phosphatidyl choline) and cholesterol may have facilitatory effects on the viral infection. Our simulations provide valuable guidance on pharmaceutical design and future research on corona virus pathology.
abstract_zh: 覆盖肺泡的肺表面活性物质（LS）是抵御空气传播病原体（如冠状病毒）的第一道屏障，可能有助于防止肺部感染。理解病毒结构单元与LS之间的相互作用对于高效的药物设计和制剂至关重要。由于LS是不可避免的接触对象，LS脂质与病毒蛋白及包膜之间的抑制性和促进性相互作用在病毒在呼吸系统中的命运中起着关键作用。在本工作中，通过多尺度分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟，我们研究了五种LS脂质与SARS-CoV2刺突蛋白受体结合域（RBD）之间的相互作用。通过进行自发蛋白-配体结合的粗粒化（CG）模拟，我们识别出RBD蛋白上的六个潜在表面活性剂结合位点（SBS）。我们发现所有表面活性剂均结合到被鉴定为脂肪酸结合位点（FABS）的结合口袋，该位点对RBD-ACE2结合具有变构效应。CG模拟揭示FABS是多种磷脂和胆固醇最可能的结合位点。随后对反向转换的CG结合构象进行的原子级模拟显示，在FABS处具有高表面活性剂结合能（27-58 kcal/mol），并且FABS结合的蛋白-表面活性剂复合物表现出表面活性剂选择性行为。我们的分析预测，虽然阴离子脂质POPG和POPI（棕榈酰油酰磷脂酰甘油/肌醇）可能具有抑制作用，但DPPC（二棕榈酰磷脂酰胆碱）和胆固醇可能对病毒感染具有促进作用。我们的模拟为药物设计和冠状病毒病理学的未来研究提供了宝贵指导。
